title: Unpacking GI-TOC's Whistleblowing Framework
report_title: A cocaine foothold in the south
summary: Maya and Daniel examine the formal Whistleblowing Policy released by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime. They discuss the scope of covered misconduct, the strict bar against anonymous claims, the specific reporting channels, and how the organization structures oversight and protections.

title: Unpacking the GI-TOC Whistleblowing Policy
report_title: COP13 backs a landmark protocol on environmental crimes, but the toughest negotiations lie ahead
summary: Maya and Daniel break down the official Whistleblowing Policy document released by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime. They examine who can report wrongdoing, the strict rules around confidentiality and anonymity, the named intake contacts, and the structural investigation process. The conversation explores how the policy handles organizational integrity, governance oversight, and protection against retaliation.

title: New Route, Old Networks: The Lobito Corridor Dilemma
report_title: Organized crime along the Lobito Corridor
summary: Maya and Daniel break down a November 2026 policy brief from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime on the Lobito Corridor. They explore how billions in Western infrastructure investment aimed at securing critical minerals risk entrenching existing criminal economies across Central Africa.

title: Central Africa's Critical Minerals and the Criminal Scramble
report_title: Who will profit from Central Africa’s critical minerals?
summary: Maya and Daniel examine a November 2026 report from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime on Central Africa's critical raw materials. They analyze how global competition for energy transition minerals is opening doors to armed conflict, geocriminality, and elite capture.

title: Unpacking the MNET-CTC Collaboration Grants Call
report_title: Calling for collaborative proposals to counter organized crime in the Mekong
summary: Maya and Daniel break down the newly published call for proposals under the Mekong Network to Counter Transnational Crime (MNET-CTC) programme, run by GI-TOC and the Australian Government. They explore the grant structure, target crime areas, community resilience focus, cross-border requirements, and key application timelines.

title: Libya: Human Smuggling Shifts East
report_title: Human smuggling and trafficking in North Africa and the Sahel - 2026
summary: Maya and Daniel break down a major monitoring brief from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime examining the changing dynamics of human smuggling in Libya across 2025 and mid-2026. They trace the geopolitical fractures, enforcement crackdowns in Tripolitania, and the dramatic eastward shift of maritime departures toward Greece.

title: Following Guyanese Gold: Crime, Power, and Illicit Flows
report_title: Illicit gold and financial flows in Guyana and Suriname
summary: Maya and Daniel examine a major investigation by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime and SWISSAID into Guyana's gold sector. They explore how elite capture, under-declaration, cross-border smuggling, and international trading hubs like the UAE fuel illicit financial flows across South America and beyond.

title: The Business of War in the Central Sahel
report_title: Central Sahel: Illicit markets and their intersection with conflict
summary: Maya and Daniel break down a landmark report from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime exploring how illicit economies fuel armed conflict across Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso. They examine the resurgence of foreign kidnap-for-ransom, the contestation of vital transport corridors, shifting artisanal gold and drug supply chains, and actionable entry points for policy intervention.

title: Inside GI-TOC's Whistleblowing Framework
report_title: A window for reform? Rethinking the UNTOC review mechanism after COP13
summary: Maya and Daniel examine the official Whistleblowing policy released by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime. They break down who can report, the strict rules around confidentiality versus anonymity, the designated intake channels, and how internal investigations are structured.

title: Inside GI-TOC's Whistleblowing Policy
summary: Maya and Daniel break down the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime's formal whistleblowing policy. They examine who can report, the explicit protections and reporting channels, how investigations are conducted, and the institutional governance designed to safeguard integrity.

title: Inside GI-TOC's Whistleblowing Framework
summary: Maya and Daniel break down the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime's formal whistleblowing policy. They examine the scope of reportable misconduct, the strict rules around confidentiality and anonymous reporting, the specific reporting channels, and how investigations and governance oversight are structured.

title: Where Next for the UNTOC? The Future of the Palermo Convention
report_title: The GI-TOC at the 13th Conference of the Parties to the UNTOC
summary: Maya and Daniel examine a briefing from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime on the future of the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC). They explore the structural delays in the convention's review mechanism, the data gap in the Global South, and the political and financial challenges facing multilateral efforts at COP13.

title: Kinship, Crime, and the Clan Debate in Germany
summary: Maya and Daniel unpack a landmark report from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime examining Arabic-speaking criminal networks in Germany. They explore the roots of long-established Mardin-origin clans, the rise of newer Syrian networks, and what law enforcement often gets wrong about kinship and organized crime.

title: Mapping Colombia's Revived Caribbean Cocaine Corridors
summary: Maya and Daniel dissect a comprehensive report from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) on how Colombian cocaine trafficking routes through the Caribbean are reviving to supply booming European markets. They explore the internal transport corridors, maritime smuggling methods, corruption dynamics, and regional geopolitical shifts detailed in the investigation.

title: Inside the Western Cape Gang Ecosystem
summary: Maya and Daniel break down Issue 10 of the Western Cape Gang Monitor by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime. They explore why military deployment under Operation Prosper is faltering, how incarcerated bosses run syndicates from their cells, the violent expansion of gangs into rural towns like Malmesbury, and the landmark trial exposing state armouries supplying the underworld.

title: Crime at a Crossroads: Eastern and South-Eastern Asia
report_title: Global Organized Crime Index 2025 - Continental overview
summary: Maya and Daniel unpack the 2025 Global Organized Crime Index report from GI-TOC focusing on Eastern and South-Eastern Asia. They examine the stark regional contrasts, the explosion of industrial cyber-scam compounds and human trafficking, and the world's widest resilience gaps.
